items.stem: What should you do first when given an open-ended ML design prompt?

options.text: Clarify functional and non-functional requirements, scale and success metrics
options.rationale: Correct: scoping requirements frames every later decision.
Design interviews are about reasoning, not coding a system.
Size is not a goal; fit to requirements is.

items.explanation: Correct: scoping requirements frames every later decision.

items.stem: Which TWO are good reasons to define a simple baseline before a complex model? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It sets a bar the complex model must beat to justify its cost
options.rationale: Correct: baselines quantify the value of added complexity.

options.text: It can ship quickly and reveal data/plumbing issues early
options.rationale: Correct: a baseline surfaces pipeline and data problems cheaply.

options.text: It guarantees the complex model is unnecessary
options.rationale: It informs, but does not guarantee, that outcome.

options.text: It removes the need for any evaluation metrics
options.rationale: Metrics are still required to compare.

items.explanation: Correct: baselines quantify the value of added complexity.

items.stem: Why discuss monitoring and A/B testing in a design interview even if asked only to 'build a recommender'?

options.text: Production ML must be measured and iterated; omitting it signals an incomplete design
options.rationale: Correct: a strong design covers the full lifecycle, not just training.
It is essential for drift and quality.

options.text: A/B testing is only for front-end colours
